subject: Startups
title: What a Pivot Actually Means
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What a Pivot Actually Means.

hook.text: Most people think a pivot means the original idea failed. Actually, it means the founder learned something new.

buildup.text: Eric Ries defined a pivot as a structured course correction to test a new hypothesis about the business.

discovery.text: A pivot keeps one foot planted. You change direction but preserve what you've learned along the way.

twist.text: The best pivots aren't desperate. They come from data—user behavior that reveals a better opportunity.

climax.text: Slack, YouTube, and Instagram all pivoted. The biggest tech companies weren't born—they were discovered.

punchline.text: A pivot isn't failure. It's insight with a new direction.

quiz.question: What defines a startup pivot?
options: A structured course correction based on new learning
